newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --
CANADA, March 3 - Montreal, Que - All terminals operating normally, no delays expected.

HONDURAS, March 3 - Puerto Cortes - Vessels berthed, 4 discharging/loading containers, 1 discharging rice, 1 discharging white corn, 1 discharging emulsified asphalt, 1 discharging fertiliser. Vessels awaiting berth, 2 to discharge/load containers, 1 to discharge fertiliser, 1 to discharge urea, 1 to discharge fuel oil, 1 to discharge bagged fertiliser/iron. Vessels due, 5 to discharge bananas, 1 passenger. 7 To load/discharge containers, 1 to discharge corn.

March 4 - Seven vessels discharging of which 2 containers/generals, 2 containers/bananas, 1 general, 1 rice, 2 fertiliser. 2 Vessels anchored of which 1 in ballast, 1 to discharge grain/soya. 15 Vessels due of which 1 passenger, 5 containers/generals, 1 generals, 4 bananas, 1 lumber, 1 fuel oil, 2 liquid chemicals, no berthing delays expected.

MEXICO, March 4 - Tampico - Vessels in port, 2 sugar, 1 repairs, 2 general cargo, 1 cement, 2 corn, 1 container. Altamira - In port, 2 containers, 2 steel coils, 1 chemical. Veracruz - In port, 3 sugar, 3 pipes, 3 grain, 1 scrap, 2 chemicals, 3 general cargo. Manzanillo - In port, 3 containers, 2 cement, 2 general cargo, 2 grain, 1 steel sheets. Coatzacoalcos - In port, 9 chemicals, 5 oil tankers. All ports working normally.

PANAMA, March 3 - The new concessionaire Panama Ports Co. (of Hutchinson Wampoa Ltd.) took over the ports at two entrances to the canal on 1/3. Cristobal - 17 Vessels in port of which 1 passenger, 4 cargo operations. Balboa - 15 Vessels in port of which 2 cargo operations. Panama Canal - Transit booking system normal (full capacity). 30 Vessels due, 33 in queue, 10 booked, 42 scheduled. Average of booked and non-booked waters time is 22-5 hours.

UNITED STATES, March 3 - Port Newark, NJ - Three vessels in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ - Four vessels in port. Bayway, NJ - One vessel in port. Honolulu, HI - Harbour - 1 Container vessel alongside, 1 tuna vessel alongside, 1 tug alongside, 4 tugs and barges alongside. Anchorage - 1 Bulk carrier, 1 tanker. Barbers Point - Two barges alongside. Offport moorings - 1 Tanker. Hampton Roads, VA - Seven general cargo/container vessels in pier operating, 2 bulkers in pier loading coal, 4 anchored waiting to load, 1 bulker loading grain, 1 tanker waiting to discharge uan solution. 11 Vessels in pier under repair, 1 bulker discharging salt, 1 loading woodpulp. Baltimore, MD - Vessels operating, 7 bulkers, 3 container vessels, 1 ro-ro, 2 auto vessels, 2 tankers, 3 general cargo, 1 cable vessel on standby. 4 Vessels in repair yard, 4 bulkers awaiting berth.

EAST COAST - Baltimore, MD - No congestion at Dundalk terminal. Clear at C and D Cal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling, average waiting time Consol Coal 5 days. No berthing congestion at liquid bulk facilities. Charleston, SC - Heavy vessel traffic expected at Columbus Street terminal, other terminals light. Oil terminals on schedule. Dredger operating in the main channel this week and will be there for approx. 2 months, all vessel traffic will be affected, but no delays at any time. Jacksonville - No heavy berth congestion. Miami, FL - No congestion. Drilling in the government cut east of the turning basin, channel will be closed for 12 hours on the following dates, 11/3 1800 to 0600, 18/3 1800 to 0600, 25/3 1800 to 0600, 1/4 1800 to 0600. New York, NY - Anchorages and sugar terminals congested, no congestion at container, tanker terminals. Philadelphia, PA - No congestion in port Camden or Wilmington. Savannah, GA - Heavy congestion at Garden City terminals during early part of the week. No delays expected

GULF COAST - Houston, TX - No congestion in city docks, Cargill, Houston public grain elevator and farmland grain elevator Galveston. Mobile, AL - Heavy fog causing delays. New Orleans, LA - No change in river level.

WEST COAST - Columbia river - 14 Grain vessels in port of which 7 loading, 7 waiting with average waiting time of 3-5 days. Coos Bay - Working normally. Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan - Berthing delays of 1-2 days. Koch Carbon - 1 Vessel due in March, no berthing delays expected. Coal/petcoke, berthing delays of 1-2 days expected. Longshore stopwork meeting from 1800 5/3 to 0300 6/3. San Francisco, CA - Two tankers have broken free at the Wickland Shelby facility as a result of the flooding and subsequent stronger currents. The shoaling at the port of stockton is still being dredged. Pilots currently moving vessels up to 1 draft of 28 ft. Fw. New soundings are expected this weekend. Seattle - Both grain elevators have a backlog of vessels at anchor awaiting berth.
